title: Terms and operations documentation still contradict the merged account and four-level product behavior

original_titles.title: Docs report stale test counts and omit six test files
Doc drift and pre-publication hazards (stale test counts; handbook example leaks a real defect)
Terms/Login copy claims accounts are created automatically on first sign-in, contradicting backend rejection of unregistered emails
EXTRA: four-level participant flow replaces the spec's Round 1/Round 2 model

problem: PR #59 corrected some README, API and security docs, but frontend Terms still says accounts may be created automatically on first sign-in. COMPETITION_RULES, PRIVACY_NOTICE and EVENT_OPERATIONS_PLAYBOOK retain invite/activation/reset routes, account-status and old single-round “do not upload code” instructions. Some known-gaps/reconciliation documents still refer to the frontend as not implemented.
impact: Organizers and participants can follow obsolete routes or misunderstand password setup, code submission, stage flow and manual test process. Operational errors become likely even when the code is correct.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Search all tracked docs and public copy for invite, activation, AUTH_NOT_ACTIVATED, status=disabled, passwordless staff, “no code upload”, v1-only workflow and removed endpoint names.
Reconcile each hit against current routes and behavior; retain historical statements only in clearly dated audit archives, not active operator instructions.
Update Terms, Competition Rules, Privacy Notice, Participant Handbook and Event Operations Playbook from one approved account/flow policy source.
Add a CI docs-link/endpoint check or a small contract test that fails when docs mention removed endpoints or claim a workflow that has no route.
Require owner review and legal review where documents describe rules, privacy, penalties or proctoring.

acceptance_criteria: No active public/operator doc instructs organizers to use removed invite/activation routes.
Participant documents describe the four-level repo/edit/upload/submit path correctly.
CI flags references to removed endpoints or stale auth codes.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

residual_risk_or_scope_note: The merged PR updated parts of the documentation, but the full repository still contains contradictory active guidance.
